facts:
## CELL FACTS

Cell 木_偏印 (Wood carrying The Alchemist). Persona The Alchemist (偏印). Definition line: "Unconventional nourishment, the insight that transmutes". Keyword Insight, charge fierce, poles catalyst Vision / friction Distance. Family function: Mind. Cost dimension: nourishment that transmutes; fed on strange food, recipe unshareable. Arena: crucible, moon-side, distillation, the changed substance. Classical portrait: unorthodox absorption; solitary mastery; intake that starves output (枭神夺食). Ruled domains: Learning, Intuition, Solitude. Sibling (other polarity of the family): 正印.
Element arena: Wood (trunk, branch, root, grain, growth, the forest). dm_element (which core reads this cell): Fire. structural_interaction seed: "Wood generating Fire same-polarity — reach as fuel sustaining warmth".
- k2_overview: "Your Wood moves as the Alchemist: knowledge grown rather than gathered. Understanding grafts onto you slowly and lives, ideas cross-pollinating in ways textbooks never planned. Your learning is a garden with strange hybrids. Tend it privately as you must, then let people taste the fruit. It is stranger and better than you think."
- k2_functional: "You think by grafting: splicing distant ideas until something new takes root."
- adj_chips: {"friction":["Tangled","Secretive","Reclusive"],"catalyst":"[REDACTED: the words under test]"}
- k2_domain_readings: {"Learning":"You learn like an ecosystem: slowly, laterally, everything connecting to everything. Formal courses feel like pots. Give yourself wild ground, mixed sources, and the hybrids will astonish.","Intuition":"Your intuition grows on the underside of awareness: a slow mycelium that suddenly fruits an answer. Give questions dormancy. What you cannot force overnight arrives by spring.","Solitude":"Your solitude is a greenhouse: ideas need protected warmth before weather. Take the seclusion without guilt. Just transplant finished thoughts outdoors. Gardens are meant to be walked in."}
- fn_reading.catalyst.ledger (three rows, index-aligned to adj_chips.catalyst; authored order is significance order):
  - row 0: [REDACTED: the target row]
  - row 1: [REDACTED: the target row]
  - row 2: [REDACTED: the target row]
- Sibling cell 木_正印 chips (nothing you write may fit the sibling): {"catalyst":["Nurturing","Evergreen","Shade-giving"],"friction":["Smothering","Clingy","Dormant"]}
- Sibling cell 木_正印 catalyst row 0 drive passage, for the sibling test on the tension (this row must name a different either-or): "Growing people is your mind’s favorite work. You see the seed version of someone, water it with patience nobody else budgets, and stand back when it takes. Half your pride lives in other people’s accomplishments, planted years earlier, never invoiced."

Core element Fire, energy element Wood. Law: Wood feeds Fire (木生火: dry branches make the flame). Relative to the core the energy is the feeder, so Wood is this core's Mind. No chart is attached to this batch: the cell is written for every chart with a Fire core that shows Wood on the catalyst pole, so no percentage and no state of one chart appears in any value. The catalyst pole of Wood as the Mind is the Underfueled band's case (the core burns more than it takes in); tone by pole: compliment. Rows: row 0, row 1, row 2, each with its three angles (drive, cost_self, cost_others: the drive, the cost to the reader, the cost to others; the app shows one angle per row by position rotation, so each passage must stand alone); one chip per row, written once and copied byte-identical onto the row's three fields. The pair cell 火_木's definition and advice for this pole are rewritten in the same batch (the pair skeleton) and are withheld here; no four-word run may be shared with them, so keep every phrase the ledger's own.

value.text: Sensing a thing first comes easier to you than waiting to be told. You sense the pause before an answer, and your guess runs past the words. What you sense first arrives ahead of your ability to say it, so let the words catch up.

value_b.text: You sense where a thing is going before anyone says it. Needing to understand ahead of being told, you take the half-sentence rather than wait on the whole. You carry what you sensed alone until someone catches on, a wait you can afford.

value.text: A thing sensed first feels safer than a plain question asked. Since you would rather sense it than be told, what you have half right stays half right. Say it out loud sometimes, because the lesson you keep missing comes to the one who asks.

value.text: Whenever someone starts telling you something, you sense its direction and answer that. Sensing the point before the words saves you time and costs the other person their own ending. Let them reach it, because you want them heard as much as understood.

value.text: You teach yourself what others take classes in. Being handed an answer never feels like knowing it, and you would rather be self-taught than shown. The self-taught way costs you time, and what you learn by it is the kind that stays.

value_b.text: The things you are best at, you taught yourself. Because a lesson only counts once you have found it yourself, you take the long way through a subject instead of the taught one. It costs you years, and you would pay them again.

value.text: You sleep on a question rather than answer on the spot. Forcing an answer now feels like lying to you, and you give the question a night first. Sleeping on it makes you the slow one in every quick exchange, and that slowness is chosen.

value_b.text: The answer you trust shows up after sleeping on it. Rather than reply with the part of you that talks, you sleep on the question and let the part that knows work. You answer last, and the fast chances go to whoever spoke first.

value.text: Sleeping on a question makes the answer real. Being sure later matters more to you than being in it now, so the opening that wanted an answer closes. You lose chances to a yes one day late, and the quick yes is yours too.

value.text: With an answer someone needs, you sleep on it before you give it. Sleeping on it matters more than a quick reply, and you leave whoever asked waiting longer. You cost them a day of wondering, and a date you name is cheaper than silence.
